flag.title: The flag
flag.teller: One of the women at the table tells you:
flag.text:
GONZALES, September 30
The flag
×

One of the women at the table tells you:

The men want a flag to go behind. It is a breadth of white cotton about six feet long, with the cannon painted on it in black and the words under it: "Come and take it." Some want a star over the gun.

The women of the town have given the cloth.

STRONGLY SUPPORTED White cotton, a black cannon and the words "Come and take it" - as two men who saw it remembered it about 1900. HIST-TEX-468
DISPUTED When it was made. The Handbook of Texas says a few days before the fight; Noah Smithwick, who saw it, remembered it made for Austin's army later in October. No letter of 1835 mentions a flag. HIST-TEX-468
DISPUTED Who made it. "History is silent on the subject" (Smithwick). Later accounts name Sarah Seely DeWitt and her daughter Eveline, or Eveline DeWitt with Cynthia Burns, or with Caroline Zumwalt, or a committee of five officers with cloth from the women of the town. HIST-TEX-468
TRADITION That it was cut from the silk wedding dress of Naomi DeWitt, who married that August. The Handbook calls the story apocryphal. HIST-TEX-468
DISPUTED The star over the gun: some who remembered it drew one, some did not. HIST-TEX-468

The people drawn here are a picture of the town, not a count of it; what they say is written for the game from what the record says happened. Anything said in a solid box is on record; a dashed box is reconstructed. The women are not named because nobody knows who they were. The game shows the flag made here on these two days because the Handbook puts it at the fight (FIC-GONZ-411).

The women at the table would take a hand with the cloth.

Ezra: Help with the flag
The women of the town are making the flag; Ezra could help the men at the blacksmith's instead.

street.title: The men come back
street.teller: Ruth Crandall, who lives on the commons, tells you:
street.text:
GONZALES, October 2
The men come back
×

Ruth Crandall, who lives on the commons, tells you:

They came back this afternoon with the cannon and the soldiers' baggage. The soldiers fired and were fired on, and then went off toward Béxar without the gun.

Not one of ours was lost. People are saying the war has begun.

DOCUMENTED The Mexican detachment withdrew toward Béxar without the cannon. HIST-GONZ-004
STRONGLY SUPPORTED The force was back in Gonzales about two in the afternoon of October 2, with the Mexican baggage, "without losing a man". HIST-TEX-465
DOCUMENTED "The rubicon is crossed" - William Fisher, writing from Gonzales to Austin on October 3. HIST-TEX-465

The people drawn here are a picture of the town, not a count of it; what they say is written for the game from what the record says happened. Anything said in a solid box is on record; a dashed box is reconstructed. Ruth Crandall is invented (FIC-GONZ-009).
